**Fixes the update check on macOS, which failed with an error about a missing ZIP file.**

## What was wrong

Asking a Mac copy to update produced `ZIP file not provided: [` and nothing else. The
sentence was accurate and described the wrong problem.

electron-updater installs macOS updates through Squirrel, which wants a `.zip`; the
release ships `.dmg` files, so it stopped there. But shipping a `.zip` as well would only
have moved the failure later. Squirrel will only swap in a build whose code signature
satisfies the running app's, and an ad-hoc signature — which is all this project has,
having no Apple Developer ID — has no identity to match on, only the bundle's own hash,
which every rebuild changes. The download would have completed and then been refused,
120MB later.

## What it does now

The app checks its own signature at startup and stops pretending. A Mac copy still tells
you a new version is out — in the notification, in the right-click and tray menus, and in
**About** — and offers the page to get it from. It no longer starts a download it cannot
finish, and **Download updates automatically** is ignored rather than quietly wasting
bandwidth on your behalf.

The check is on the signature, not on the operating system: a build signed with a real
Developer ID updates itself normally, so this reverts on its own the day there is one.

Windows is unaffected and updates as before.

## Downloads

| Platform              | File                           |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| Windows 10 / 11       | `Claude-Usage-Setup-1.2.1.exe` |
| macOS — Apple silicon | `Claude-Usage-1.2.1-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS — Intel         | `Claude-Usage-1.2.1-x64.dmg`   |

macOS refuses the first launch of an unsigned download — *"Claude Usage is damaged and
can't be opened"*. It is not damaged; that is the quarantine flag, and clearing it is one
command:

```bash
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/Claude Usage.app"
```
